name: Skank

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in Jamaican dance halls in the 1950s and 1960s.
It was later adopted by British mods and skinheads in the 1960s and saw a resurgence during the 2 Tone era of the 1970s and 1980s.
on_screen: Map: Jamaica · Global

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It serves as a consensual release of emotion.
The community maintains a safety-first approach, where dancers protect those who fall in the pit.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance features a running-man leg motion combined with alternating bent-elbow fist-punches.
Variations include the punk-style two-stepping, the restrained reggae stroll, and the technical x-stepping found in drum and bass.
Watch for Stroll, Two-stepping.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (km6Zyw81pP4)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Dancers often form a circle or a 'pit'.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Ska music, characterized by a prominent backbeat on the second and fourth beats of a 4/4 bar, is the primary musical accompaniment.
The dance is also performed to reggae, hardcore punk, and drum and bass.
Listen for the Electric guitar.
The pulse is 4/4.
The music is defined by a strong backbeat played by the electric guitar on the second and fourth beats of a 4/4 bar.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The band Big D and the Kids Table is noted for popularizing the 'stroll' variation.
Variations include the reggae-style stroll, the punk-style two-stepping, and the drum and bass-style x-stepping.
The dance evolved from Jamaican ska roots through British mod and skinhead subcultures into modern punk and electronic music scenes.
